concept.name: Log loss
concept.definition: A proper scoring loss equal to the negative log probability assigned to the observed class, averaged across observations.
concept.intuition: It summarizes one aspect of prediction error or decision quality in a number or curve.
concept.mechanics: Clip probabilities away from zero for numerical safety, select the probability of each observed class, take negative logs, and average.
concept.formula: Binary log loss = -mean(y log p + (1-y) log(1-p))
concept.failure_modes: Class imbalance, threshold choice, unequal error costs, outliers, and dependence can make the summary inappropriate or unstable.
concept.misconceptions: No single metric captures economic utility, turnover, risk, calibration, and trading costs at once.
concept.example: A 0.8 forecast for an event that occurs incurs loss -log(0.8), about 0.223.
